questions.question: Insolation reaches the top of the atmosphere at roughly the same rate everywhere. Why then do the tropics receive far more heating per square metre?
options: The angle of incidence is high near the equator, so the same beam lands on a small area, while oblique polar rays spread the same energy over a much larger area
The sun is physically closer to the equator

questions.question: The 'path length' penalty at high latitudes means that:
options: Rays travel further from the sun to the poles
Oblique rays slant through a far greater thickness of atmosphere, so more energy is scattered, reflected and absorbed before reaching the surface
Polar air is thicker than tropical air
The poles receive no radiation in winter

questions.question: Approximate albedo values quoted in the lesson are:
options: Fresh snow and ice roughly 80–90%, open ocean under 10%

questions.question: Of the insolation arriving at the top of the atmosphere, the lesson's budget gives roughly:
options: 10% reflected, 10% absorbed by the atmosphere, 80% at the surface
Half reflected and half absorbed by the atmosphere
About 30% reflected to space, about 20% absorbed by the atmosphere, about half absorbed at the surface

subtopics.title: The Axis, the Revolution and the Seasons

questions.question: The earth's axis is tilted:
options: 23,5 degrees from the vertical, and holds that lean in a fixed direction all year (parallelism)
66,5 degrees from the vertical, changing direction each season
It is not tilted; the orbit is tilted

questions.question: On about 22 December the overhead sun is at:
options: The Tropic of Capricorn, 23,5 degrees south — South Africa's summer solstice, longest day
The Tropic of Cancer, 23,5 degrees north

questions.question: Cape Town lies at 34 degrees south. Its midday solar altitude on 21 June (declination 23,5 degrees north) is:
A learner writes that we have winter because the earth is further from the sun. Why does this lose the mark?
options: The earth's orbit is a perfect circle
The earth is furthest from the sun in December
The earth is actually CLOSEST to the sun in early January, during our summer and Europe's winter — seasons are caused by the axial tilt, not distance

subtopics.title: How Energy Moves Through the Atmosphere

questions.question: Feeling warmth on your face while standing near coals without touching them demonstrates:
options: Radiation — energy transferred as electromagnetic waves, needing no medium

questions.question: Why is conduction a poor explanation for heating anywhere above the lowest few centimetres of the atmosphere?
options: Air is a poor conductor, so molecule-to-molecule transfer is confined to air in direct contact with a hot surface such as Kalahari sand

questions.question: The afternoon sea breeze pushing cool marine air into Durban is an example of:
options: Advection — the horizontal transfer of heat by moving air or water

questions.question: Latent heat is described as the 'quiet giant' because:
options: Evaporating a kilogram of water absorbs about 2,5 megajoules with no temperature rise; the energy travels inside the vapour and is released far away and high up when condensation occurs

subtopics.title: Surplus, Deficit and the Global Heat Engine

questions.question: The energy SURPLUS zone lies approximately:
options: Between 40 degrees north and 40 degrees south, where absorbed shortwave exceeds longwave lost to space
Poleward of 60 degrees in each hemisphere

questions.question: The strongest evidence that energy MUST be transported poleward is:
options: The equator-to-pole temperature difference stays broadly stable from decade to decade instead of the tropics heating and the poles cooling without limit

questions.question: The split of poleward heat transfer between the two carriers is roughly:
options: Atmosphere about three-quarters, oceans about one-quarter

questions.question: South Africa's two coastal currents illustrate the correction because:
options: The warm Agulhas Current carries tropical heat south along the east coast while the cold Benguela Current draws polar water north along the west coast

questions.question: Tilting the torch turns the tight bright circle into a big dim oval because:
options: The same amount of light is shared over a much larger area of wall — exactly what happens to sunlight at high latitudes
The torch battery weakens when tilted
The wall reflects more light when tilted
Tilting makes the light travel further from the battery

questions.question: The 'crowded taxi rank' comparison explains:
options: Path length — slanting sunlight pushes through far more air, losing energy to scattering, reflection and absorption the whole way

questions.question: The black bakkie and white bakkie comparison stands for:
options: Albedo — bright ice and snow bounce most sunlight away, while the dark ocean absorbs almost all of it

subtopics.title: The Ball That Never Straightens Up

questions.question: In the leaning-ball demonstration, the rule 'never straighten it and never turn the lean around' represents:
options: Parallelism of the earth's axis — the lean stays fixed in direction all year, which is what produces the seasons
The rotation of the earth on its axis
The elliptical shape of the orbit
The tilt slowly reversing each season

questions.question: Cape Town's midday sun swings from about 79,5 degrees in December to about 32,5 degrees in June. The full effect on heating is:
options: A 47-degree drop in sun height PLUS about four and a half hours less daylight — weaker energy delivered for fewer hours
A 47-degree drop, but daylight stays the same

questions.question: Around 21 March and 23 September:
options: The sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer
The southern hemisphere has its longest day
The lamp shines square on the ball's middle — the sun is overhead at the equator and day and night are equal everywhere
The earth is closest to the sun

questions.question: The strongest proof that distance does NOT cause the seasons is:
options: The orbit is a perfect circle
The earth spins once a day
We are closest to the sun in early January, which is our summer but Europe's deep winter — one distance cannot make both

subtopics.title: Kettle, Braai and Taxi — Moving Heat

questions.question: Picking up the metal grid handle left on the fire and burning your fingers demonstrates:
options: Conduction — heat passing by direct touch, molecule to molecule

questions.question: The shimmer rising straight up off the coals, scaled up to Highveld size, produces:
options: Convection — warm air rising until it condenses into cumulonimbus and delivers the late-afternoon thunderstorm

questions.question: Feeling cold when a breeze passes over your sweaty skin illustrates:
options: Latent heat — turning water into vapour steals heat from your skin and carries it away invisibly

questions.question: In the spaza-shop picture of the energy balance:
options: The poles have the surplus and the tropics the deficit
The tropics are the shop with surplus bread, the poles the shop with a deficit, and the winds carry about three loaves in four while ocean currents carry the rest
